title: Am I the only one with minimal Claude subscription developing a full game slowly ?
author: Dangerous-Tower-8814
selftext:
I've been working for more than a year on a multiplayer game on Unreal with the minimal Claude subscription. This doesn't create game that fast ! I mean... 5 to 10 time faster than before but I see tones of posts about game made in 24h and tones of shitty AI games on Steam.

Is this how do you use AI ?

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body: It'll be done when it's done. You should find out how much people that "finish" building games in 24 hours spend, it's a flex for them, but I'm unsure whom they're flexing at.

replies.author: velocimposter
replies.body: I'm impressed at the technology, but not the person behind the prompt.  From a gamedev perspective one shots go into my mental trash bin and set on fire.

replies.author: misteryk
replies.body: even with AI as good as it is now the game made in 24h must be a real slop. i spend like half of the time just playing a game so find small things that need QoL like better filters/sorting items or making gear presets

comments.author: Shrineheart
comments.body: I'm on the lowest plan and up until this year it was mostly documents and a couple of false starts with different game engines. Now there's a proper game loop happening. I will say Claude code seems to use up much less than Claude projects etc.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body: I have $20 Claude plan, $20 GPT plan and $5 promo gemini.  that gets me everything I need to work quite a bit. I try to be token efficient, and just do one small bit at a time. I may my weekly usage every week, and come out way ahead in terms of token usage vs API.

replies.author: OneNpcAmongOthers
replies.body: What do you use the different plans for? I have only used Claude for programming so far and would like to hear how and why you choose to manage multiple subs

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body:
I use Claude opus 5.5 for most programing tasks. I do have it use blender MCP sometimes. I use Astra 6.2 and Gemini Neon to use Blender MCP for low and mid poly assets to feed into my project.  
  
I have tried neon out when I ran out of claude usage, and it did pretty good with the code actually, and worked faster than claude.   
  
I sometimes use astra or neon as an adversarial code reviewer as well, but I have an engineer working with me that does that too.

replies.author: J0rdian
replies.body: How do you use Neon. I thought it wasn't available for the 5 dollar plan? I have the same plan and just use it for animations with their video model

replies.author: Maple-Syrup89
replies.body:
I got a special promo rate for pro. And then I decided it was useful enough that I bought a year for $100.  

I have used it for a couple videos to give to claud to make frame by frame animations.

But I use it mostly for the blender MCP right now, and a bit for code.

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: I have two $20 subscriptions. I alternate and it works well. I don’t always fully use up the usage, but it’s nice when I max one out after a few days.

comments.author: roodammy44
comments.body: I’m on the lowest plan. I don’t see how you can be on a higher when everything it makes is kinda broken and needs a ton of fixes. But maybe it’s cos I don’t have a ton of time

comments.author: PatchyWhiskers
comments.body: A lot of people are spending thousands a month on games that don’t have a potential to make thousands. I think that after spending $1000 in tokens and $100 on Steam to make an average of $200, people who just want a side hustle are going to move onto something more profitable.

comments.author: CoffeeCup220
comments.body: Sly and shitty way to advertise, instead.

comments.author: h1soft
comments.body:
Same here, solo on a mobile roguelike with Claude Code writing most of the GDScript. The code part got fast, but that didn't make the game fast. The slow part is still playing it over and over and figuring out why something feels wrong, and no model does that for you.

The "made in 24h" posts mostly show that something runs, not that it's fun. A year on a multiplayer Unreal game sounds pretty normal to me.

replies.author: solo-unicorn
replies.body: Or they want you to buy there course

replies.author: Further_Beyond
replies.body:
I’m 1 month in on Claude pro and about 15-20% done with my Pokemon but football instead of Pokemon battles game lol.

I did sign up for Gemini pro with it being $5 for 3 months on Thanksgiving and I really like Neon’s model. Plus the usage is so so so so so much better than Claude.

comments.author: Drachis
comments.body: I have been exploring developing game ideas with Claude and pico8 to create prototypes.  Can usually get a reasonably polished game loop in 24 hours on the 20$ plan.  Content is the biggest hurdle for getting it visually shippable. Overall it's been fun but nothing AAA scale, closer to game jam.

comments.author: ArtemisWingz
comments.body:
The people who "Finish" a game in 24 hours are not making full games.

They are making glorified demos that lack any real depth and are surface level games that won't sell because it's just a remake of anything dumbed down boring click bait game.

An "Endless runner" game isn't impressive, or the 206899647th Roguelike that has no depth what so ever won't see sales. Or that platformer that's worse than a 1980s platformer isn't doing anything new.

Small games in a day are not innovative and big games are just demo level that has no depth or story.

You taking a year to work on a game is actually something to brag about as you are taking rime to add heart and soul to the game. (Without A.I. it might of taken you 3 to 4)

comments.author: BirdiePeep
comments.body:
I'm on the $20 a month plan and this is everything I need.  I come from game and software development so It's easier for me to describe what I want and how I want it built, which means I save on a lot of token use.  Honestly this is already a blazing speed of development for me and I wouldn't want to go any faster.  I like working on each small chunk as I need it.

I think a lot of people blazing through max subscriptions are giving vauge or very large asks, expecting agents to fill in the details.  It might produce something, and maybe that works for them, but I enjoy the development process.

comments.author: Another_3
comments.body: >\-Laughs in free claude

replies.author: Another_3
replies.body: Yeah. I barely do stuff on a regular 9-5  shift day. Just on days off. I read and ask to explain all code and I also start with a skeleton of what i want and i build piece by piece. No rush, once i start with assets i will use local AIs. I ask chat gpt lots of questions as it has unlimited text msg and i have gemini pro at work which i sometimes use to do some research and planning.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body:
Yeah basically, if you were a gamedev before. And you want more control that actually works.  
Up until recently AI caused a bit of a mess sometimes. So I just coded manually, and then asked chatgpt for small tasks, and structs and functions here and there. Though at the moment its quite good, but that is still an option.

The recent project im in, AI just created a mess of an architecture. So yeah.

comments.author: fukinuhhh
comments.body: Same here, I usually meet the weekly limit in 2-3 days

comments.author: schmighaar
comments.body: Not the only one

comments.author: pharodrum
comments.body: Nope, I'm taking my time and being thorough with a lot of planning between each step. Usually hit my limit by Thursday and have to wait until Sunday but I plan and work on assets. Plenty of other things to do.

comments.author: Nooberling
comments.body: Games require time and a ton of QA.

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body:
I’m building several games of different genres. The simpler games - mobile, casual, arcade, card, etc, can be really fast to make. If you keep the AI default’s UX, it’s pretty much running in a few hours. Tuning the gameplay might be a few more weeks, depending on how much refinement you find necessary.

The bigger the scope, the more the tuning needs. An RPG? Real-time synchronous multiplayer with different combat types and power scaling and character skills and equipment (weapons, armor, ‘dodge’, etc) - lots and lots of tuning and polish.

If you’re doing a moderately complicated game design, in your spare time, on the Claude Pro plan, yeah it will probably take over a year.

comments.author: ohThisUsername
comments.body: Me, I subscribe to Gemini and I just keep going until I hit my limit and then wait for the refresh

comments.author: intLeon
comments.body: Weekly usage is shit with bigger packages anyway.. same here!

comments.author: sapinhosapao
comments.body: I just have Claude Pro (20$/m) that i split with work and recently Free trial with Chat GPT plus for 1 month that allow to improve a little bit the graphics (Claude is very bad at them) and let me work on Nintendo 3ds port along. It gives you time to think and test with time, so you get new ideas along the way.

comments.author: StellarSoupStudio
comments.body: Right there with you, I'm currently in the phase of trying to make the controls intuitive for mouse and keyboard lol. That and pestering anyone I can to try and play it 😅

comments.author: NightZonic
comments.body: Using an engine slows things down. Even with CLI or MCP. Instead just use code and raw libraries, or frameworks like monogame or brutal. LLMs understand code naturally rather than going through the intermediary or a MCP. The token use is more efficient and faster. You can ask the agent to make your own editor tools, plus they’ll be customised to your game. Plus my C# games build and run in a second. Unity claims to be so much faster with domain reloading improvements but it’s still at least 10 seconds to even test your game. Unreal can be worse. Fast/instant reloading is so much better for fast iteration, and for agents running tests in the background. I’m never going back to Unity’s slow builds

comments.author: Soggy-Number1436
comments.body: I dont even pay for claude at all im just using the free version and adding small amounts of code every day without trying to rush through making the game. Its been 2 weeks of dev and 10 days of actually starting to make the game andi basically only have movement and money in the game.

replies.author: Rhytmik
replies.body: Lol same. After a month of iterations i had a browser prototype. Moving now to unreal engine and after 3 days i finally have a simple UI. Free life is slow but its still progress towards my own dream game.

replies.author: The8Darkness
replies.body: Ngl that sounds like it would take a lifetime for a game.

replies.author: PM_Me_Those_
replies.body: Yea i mean that will take as long as solo devwork normally did, decades.

replies.author: Codacc69420
replies.body: Using the free sub feels ok but once you’ve tried the paid version you won’t be able to go back

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I think the first 5% percent of building my game def took the longest. Ai wasn’t very good at code like a year ago and besides that just like deciding very basic things like what engine be should I use, how big will the player be, what’s the color palette, what size will I render, how do I architect, what is my naming conventions for files. Shit took a while to get going and I gave up twice with month breaks inbetween I was going so slow. Wayyy different a year in. And I don’t often use that much ai. Mostly for code, it’s all isolated and it’s usually done quick and on the first pass.

replies.author: AEsylumProductions
replies.body: I don't know how you can do that without Projects, that's hardcore

comments.author: robobax
comments.body: I am building methodically and slowly. So yes.

comments.author: skyline79
comments.body: Same. I use the chat part of Claude to get into the details of the entire game. Only when I know exactly what I want to get done, will I paste into Claude code. Always mindful of usage credits, and let chat/code know accordingly.

comments.author: x2manypips
comments.body: The pro is enough for hobbyists

comments.author: Hanzimer
comments.body: in 24h you can probably make Tetris clone not a decent multiplayer game, with or without AI. Generally, the ideas come out while developing so developing little pieces it's ever a better idea than just asking: "make a multiplayer game".

comments.author: Dweebiechimp
comments.body: If you don't 1 shot it with fable overnight while you sleep it's trash! /s

comments.author: CordouroyStilts
comments.body:
Im on the $20 Claude subscription and treat the weekly usage limit like a writer would treat a daily word count goal.  If I don't Max it out every week I'm a loser.

I also offload some simpler tasks to local LLMs on my machine to save on tokens.  They even help me generate more efficient prompts for Claude.

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body: I’m about 8 months in with Claude pro and I’m only about a third of the way done but the first few months where just making an asset builder. I’ll have a beta soon with like 215 equitable items and 20 something characters tho so I’m finally making real progress and I’m happy with it

comments.author: lighting828
comments.body: In building a triology of games on the pro subscription myself. Slow but steady

comments.author: goblingamescompany
comments.body: I started this way until about 2 months ago when I hit "the last 20%" and then I justified the upgrade from Pro to Max to push to the finish line, help with marketing/content, and work in the next game 😄

comments.author: Shppo
comments.body: yes - im cooking with 2 ultra plans 24/7

comments.author: Knoblauch12
comments.body: Controversial opinion here but I’m doing the same with Gemini but moving pretty fast on a 3D survival game with no prior game dev experience.

comments.author: Jonsotheraccount79
comments.body: You guys are killing me lol. I blew 27% of a $200 Claude plan today running 25 Fable threads in parallel doing specifications for opus and sonnet to write the code the rest of the week lol.

comments.author: nadishuddhi
comments.body: I'm doing AI assisted game dev, so I'm doing quite a bit of coding and other things by hand, so... So far the $20 a month plan is blowing my mind. It saves me so much time debugging my code and fixing little mistakes I made. I guess it depends on if you're 100% vibe coding or just using it as an assistant.

comments.author: HurryOne
comments.body: I'm on $20 chatgpt/codex. I just use it to find bugs and help with optimization and sometimes guidance on coding.

comments.author: Lumpy_Conference6640
comments.body: I am! I have a schedule thing

comments.author: No_Flow9734
comments.body: Slow and steady. Wont have anything to show for maybe 3 more months. Have spent about 1 month ish.

comments.author: lefix
comments.body: I’m building my own art, my own scenes, my own prefabs, I wire everything up myself. I’ve been working with Unity for about 15 years, I know it by heart and I can tell Claude exactly what to do. I only use it as a coding assistant, and I still write/change some code myself. I use less than half of my weekly limits. The way I see it, spending less time coding allows me to spend more time making art.

comments.author: atbrock87
comments.body: I’m doing the same exact thing! I get about 1/2 the week through using Claude, run out of usage, use the remaining 1/2 of the week to think through, plan, test, I usually keep 3-4 percent to converse with during this planning phase. Been doing that since May. Most of it has been re-iterations of previous plans, but things have been slowly coming together! I’ve been thinking about posting on here but first I want to get the main loop working bug-free, and have limited testing done first.

comments.author: Drunkendrakon6
comments.body: The key to good quality is lots of human intervention in all aspects. While you can get a decent game from simply letting AI do all the work start to finish you can never truly make something truly great. Slotbound took like 8 months and made 1.3million while using AI start to finish so do take your time. You can't rush greatness.

comments.author: Post-reality
comments.body: I spend $500-$1000 a month, working 18 hours per day on it. It may be ready for release within 2-3 years. But then again, I'm not trying to make a mobile, casual copycat/clone of something else, but something super original that hasn't been done before, neither visually nor gameplay wise.
